reason: Every BoundedTrustCache lock goes through recover() = PoisonError::into_inner (trust_plane/trust_cache.rs:97-101); clear() takes its guard that way and always marks entries invalidated (trust_cache.rs:368-380), so the FlushAll drained in apply_pending_invalidations (trust_plane/push_trust.rs:79-101) is always applied. The 'pushes exposure toward the worst case' limb is closed: clear() keeps each entry's expiry and store() uses an invalidated entry's expiry as a ceiling (trust_plane/trust_cache.rs:269-295, 356-380), witnessed by a_flush_never_extends_a_cached_bindings_deadline (push_trust.rs:370-405) and a_flush_cannot_lengthen_a_cached_bindings_deadline (trust_cache.rs:806). The 'cannot revoke faster than the file reload' fact is inherent and now stated in code (invalidation_channel.rs:38-43; revocation_tier.rs:159-166; fleet line trust_plane/mod.rs:438-455). But the row's operator limb (an incident responder INCRs believing it is the fast revocation path; the ACTIVE line is literally true and operationally misleading) survives on two operator surfaces the first pass did not check, or dismissed as wording.
missed_residue: docs/fleet-deployment-guide.md:161-170 tells operators that on INCR 'every replica flushes its trust cache on the next request and re-resolves live' (a mechanism that no longer exists: the poll is a 5s background poller) and gives the trust key-status bound as 'near-zero when the trust-epoch source is healthy' with no --trust re-read floor, i.e. it presents the epoch as the fast revocation path for a --trust key, which invalidation_channel.rs:38-43 says it is not (delivered window is R + T, worst budget x R + T). The push-ACTIVE startup line trust_plane/mod.rs:400-405 likewise says 'the trust cache flushes within one poll interval of an epoch advance' without the store qualifier. Doc/claim correction, severity low.
